claims.statement: All approved biologics and tofacitinib are superior to placebo for induction and maintenance — this is the guideline's only strong recommendation
claims.evidence_excerpt: 16 RCTs pooled. Induction (6-8 weeks) RR vs. placebo: infliximab 2.85 (2.11-3.86), adalimumab 1.62 (1.15-2.29), golimumab 2.49 (1.58-3.93), vedolizumab 2.22 (1.36-3.64), tofacitinib 3.22 (2.03-5.08), ustekinumab 2.91 (1.72-4.94). claims.statement: In biologic-naïve patients, infliximab or vedolizumab are preferred over adalimumab — based on network meta-analysis and the VARSITY head-to-head trial
claims.evidence_excerpt: VARSITY trial (vedolizumab vs. adalimumab head-to-head): clinical remission at week 52 — 34.2% vedolizumab vs. 24.3% adalimumab (RR 1.41; 1.10-1.81) among biologic-naïve patients. Network meta-analysis of 15 RCTs (3747 biologic-naïve patients): infliximab superior to adalimumab (OR 2.10; 1.16-3.79)....

claims.statement: Early biologics are suggested over gradual step-up after 5-ASA failure in high-risk patients — but the evidence is entirely indirect
claims.evidence_excerpt: No studies directly compared early biologics vs. step-up therapy. Three studies compared thiopurines vs. 5-ASA in corticosteroid-exposed patients; thiopurines achieved higher corticosteroid-free remission rates. claims.statement: In infliximab-exposed patients (especially primary non-responders), ustekinumab or tofacitinib are preferred over vedolizumab or adalimumab

claims.statement: Vedolizumab and tofacitinib are effective for induction, including in anti-TNF-exposed patients; both earn strong recommendations
claims.evidence_excerpt: GEMINI 1: vedolizumab week 6 clinical remission 16.9% vs 5.4% placebo (P=0.001); mucosal healing 40.9% vs 24.8%. Post-hoc analysis confirmed efficacy in anti-TNF failures.
